evidence.quote: Therefore, the presence or absence of the HCO$^+$ gas gaps in the HL Tau disk is still uncertain.

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image 1.1 mm continuum and HCO+ (3-2)

method.value: CASA pipeline plus manual flagging, phase self-cal, tclean with Briggs weighting, uvcontsub for continuum-subtracted cube

evidence.quote: We generated images from the calibrated visibilities with the Briggs weighting with a robust parameter of 0.5

evidence.quote: which is consistent with our observational measurement at 1.1 mm within 10%

analysis_steps.goal: Measure stellar mass and systemic velocity

method.value: Search for the Keplerian velocity pattern maximizing the S/N of the velocity-aligned stacked spectra, with absorption channels masked and only the blueshifted region (PA 48-228 deg) used

evidence.loc: Analysis, Stellar mass and systemic velocity
evidence.quote: $M_\star$ and $V_{\rm sys}$ can be estimated by searching for a velocity pattern of Keplerian rotation that maximizes the S/N of the velocity-aligned stacked spectra

key_parameters.value: free parameters M_star, V_sys; PA 138 deg, i 47 deg fixed

evidence.quote: The free parameters in the analysis are $M_\star$ and $V_{\rm sys}$.
The velocity patterns of Keplerian rotation were computed with the assumption of a geometrically thin disk.

fitting.value: S/N maximization of velocity-aligned stacked spectra; uncertainty from data noise only

evidence.quote: These estimated uncertainties in $M_\star$ and $V_{\rm sys}$ only include the uncertainty due to the noise in the data.

validation.value: Compared with previous 1.8 Msun from 13CO/C18O PV diagram; added a few percent for emitting height

evidence.quote: we estimate $M_\star$ to be 2.1$\pm$0.2 $M_\odot$.

analysis_steps.goal: Radial profiles of HCO+ (3-2) and (3-2)/(1-0) intensity ratio

method.value: Velocity-aligned stacked spectra in radial bins, Gaussian fits to (3-2), integrate both lines within 1 sigma line width, ratio in K km/s

evidence.quote: we integrated the velocity-aligned stacked spectra of the HCO$^+$ (3–2) and (1–0) emission over the channels within the 1$\sigma$ Gaussian line width from the centroid velocity

key_parameters.value: radial bin width 0.05"; innermost radius = beam 0.1" (14 au)

evidence.quote: The radius of the innermost bin is adopted to be the beam size of 0.1$''$ (14 au)

assumptions.value: (3-2) and (1-0) trace the same volume; ratio constant within each bin

evidence.quote: we assume that the HCO$^+$ (3–2) and (1–0) emission lines trace the same volume in the HL Tau disk

evidence.loc: Analysis, HCO$^+$ density and temperature profiles
evidence.quote: For each radial bin, we fitted a Gaussian line profile to the velocity-aligned stacked spectrum of the HCO$^+$ (3–2) emission.

method.value: tau_d = -ln(1 - I/(B(Td)-B(Tbg))) using azimuthally averaged continuum profiles at 1.1 and 2.9 mm

evidence.quote: Then we derived the radial profiles of the optical depths of the continuum emission ($\tau_{\rm d}$) with the radiative transfer equation
cosmic microwave background temperature of 2.73 K

analysis_steps.goal: Solve for HCO+ column density and Tex per radial bin

method.value: Three-layer radiative transfer model (dust midplane, HCO+ above and below) solved for (3-2) and (1-0) intensities

evidence.quote: We adopt a simple three-layer model of the dust and HCO$^+$ gas distributions to correct the effect of the dust opacity on the line intensity

key_parameters.value: unknowns: column density and Tex; same Tex for both lines

evidence.quote: For each radial bin, there are two unknowns, the column density and $T_{\rm ex}$ of HCO$^+$

assumptions.value: Tex equal for both lines (RADEX thermalized for n_H2>1e8 cm-3, 20-60 K); geometrically thin

evidence.quote: HCO$^+$ is thermalized when the H$_2$ number density is higher than 10$^8$ cm$^{-3}$ at a temperature of 20–60 K

fitting.value: MPFIT minimization; solutions exactly reproduce observed intensities

evidence.quote: For all radial bins, the solutions, which exactly reproduce the observed intensities, were successfully obtained

method.value: Gap depth = column density in gap over power-law interpolation from 17 and 37 au; fit self-similar accretion disk profile; power-law Tex fit

evidence.quote: the depth of this HCO$^+$ gas gap is estimated to be 4–8

assumptions.value: constant HCO+ abundance between 17 and 37 au

evidence.quote: Assuming that the HCO$^+$ abundance is constant at radii between 17 au and 37 au

fitting.value: self-similar solution; points between 20 and 35 au excluded

evidence.quote: Excluding the data points at radii between 20 au and 35 au, which belong to the inner gap

method.value: Peak positions in moment 0 fit with piecewise polynomials; PV diagram along spiral fitted with infall plus rotation model with q = -1

evidence.quote: We assume that the rotation of the spiral structure has a conserved angular momentum, meaning that $q = -1$.

assumptions.value: spiral lies in the disk mid-plane

evidence.quote: we assume that the spiral structure is in the mid-plane of the disk

fitting.value: direct fit to local peaks in PV diagram

evidence.quote: We fitted Eq. [\[vspiral\]](#vspiral) to the representative data points from the P–V diagram

method.value: Kanagawa15 formula with depth 4-8, M_star 2.1 Msun, T 60 K, alpha 1e-3

evidence.quote: a gas temperature of 60 K, and a viscosity $\alpha$ of 10$^{-3}$

evidence.loc: Discussion, Gap opened by a planet?

findings_qualitative.value: HCO+ (3-2) is optically thick (tau 2.5 to >10) except in the inner gap where tau is near 1

evidence.quote: the HCO$^+$ (3–2) line is optically thick with $\tau_{\rm g}$ ranging from 2.5 to $>$10 at the peak velocity

claims.hypothesis: Is there an HCO+ gas gap coincident with the dust gap at 30 au?
claims.experiment: LTE analysis of HCO+ (3-2) and (1-0) with continuum opacity correction
claims.result: Column density drops by 4-8 at 30 au; no other clear gap
claims.finding: HCO+ gas gap coincident with the dust gap at 30 au

evidence.quote: An HCO$^+$ gas gap at a radius of 30 au, where the column density drops by a factor of 4–8, is found

claims.hypothesis: What is the stellar mass from the resolved Keplerian rotation?
claims.experiment: Velocity-aligned stacking in the blueshifted region
claims.finding: Disk in Keplerian rotation around a 2.1 Msun star

evidence.quote: the stellar mass is estimated to be 2.1$\pm$0.2 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$

claims.hypothesis: Could a planet open the 30 au HCO+ gap?
claims.experiment: Kanagawa15 formula using gap depth, Tex and alpha
claims.finding: Planet-opened gap is plausible, but chemical effects such as UV excess are not excluded

evidence.quote: could be opened by a gas giant planet with a mass of 0.5–0.8 $M_{\rm J}$

claims.experiment: PV along the spiral compared with Keplerian rotation and infall plus rotation model
claims.result: Spiral more redshifted than Keplerian beyond 0.3"
claims.finding: Infalling and rotating gas stream toward inner disk

evidence.quote: The observed velocity structures along the spiral suggest an infalling and rotating gas stream toward the inner disk.

why_this_data.value: HCO+ (3-2) is brighter than (1-0) and adding it allows Tex and column density to be derived

evidence.quote: Thus, observations in the HCO$^+$ (3–2) line can have better S/N.

why_this_method.value: Asymmetric emission prevents a kinematic model fit, so stacking was used

evidence.quote: it is not straightforward to construct a kinematical model to fit the observed velocity channel maps.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO depletion, ionization rate enhancement and free-fall of a clump rejected for the gap and spiral

evidence.quote: Thus, the presence of the HCO$^+$ gas gap at a radius of 30 au in the HL Tau disk is not caused by the CO depletion.

limitations_admitted.value: Spiral velocities depend on the assumed mid-plane location and conserved angular momentum

evidence.quote: If the spiral structure is not in the disk mid-plane or the angular momentum is not conserved, the derived profiles of the infalling and rotational velocities are not valid.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner-radius line width overestimated, so column density, Tex and tau at the inner radius may be underestimated

evidence.quote: the column density, $T_{\rm ex}$, and $\tau_{\rm g}$ at the inner radius can be underestimated.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gap depth depends on the assumed constant HCO+ abundance and the three-layer geometry
Planet mass relies on a vertically isothermal formula and an assumed alpha
Uncertainties on stellar mass are only noise-based plus an ad hoc few percent
Stacked HCO+ (1-0) S/N is low and its profile is derived from the ratio
